title: Understanding SVD Components
text: The Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) of a matrix X is given by X=U*Σ*V**T. Here, U and $$V^T$$ are orthogonal matrices, and Σ is a diagonal matrix containing the singular values.

title: Role of Σ in SVD
text: The Σ matrix contains the singular values, which are crucial for determining the principal components. However, the principal components themselves are derived from the columns of U.

title: Principal Components from U
text: The columns of the U matrix in the SVD represent the principal components of the data. Even without Σ, U still contains the directions of maximum variance.

title: Can we find the principal components?
text: Given that U contains the principal components, can we still find them without Σ?
